message_source_quote: The Raman white-bear paper showed that the direction must tap into the concept-maintenance axis (maintain vs suppress a named concept), not just any processing-mode difference.
writeup_source_quote: The starting point was Raman et al.'s **white-bear steering** (`papers/raman2026-white-bear-steering.md`), which builds a direction from the *directed_modulation* bench family's "think about / do not think about" items and applies it at L20–24 with a large dose.

claims_about_writeup.why: The write-up does contain a description of the method and a comparison table/section (Result table comparing baseline, white-bear, think/don't-think, and remember/forget).

claims_about_writeup.quote: vectors.pt`: `{20: tensor[2560], 22: tensor[2560], 24: tensor[2560]}` for `--positions prefix --scale 1.0`
claims_about_writeup.why: Matches the write-up's final paragraph verbatim description of the vectors and their intended usage.

differences.what: The write-up notes that the self-authored think/don't-think variant—the closest competitor to remember/forget and the one most similar to white-bear—is 'methodologically close to the original' (i.e., shares white-bear's instruction verb), a caveat that tempers the novelty claim for the remember/forget method's superiority. The message omits this caveat and only states that remember/forget 'works better than think/don't think about', framing novelty more cleanly without the write-up's acknowledgment of the closely-related precursor.
differences.message_quote: My contribution is showing that **"remember/forget"** (engaging the memory system) works better than "think/don't think about" (engaging the attention system) — cosine 0.78–0.89 to white-bear, but pass@10 of 0.706 vs 0.510.
differences.writeup_quote: Self-authored think/don't-think** (same instruction verb as white-bear, different concepts): works (0.64 at scale 8) but is methodologically close to the original.

rationale: Both documents explicitly name and credit Raman et al.'s white-bear steering as the starting point the method builds on, reporting the same cosine similarity range (0.78–0.89) and framing the remember/forget contrast as a variant that taps the same concept-maintenance axis via a different (memory vs attention) pathway. The main gap is that the write-up also discloses an intermediate, more directly comparable baseline (self-authored think/don't-think, 0.637, explicitly flagged as 'methodologically close to the original') which the message's novelty pitch skips, instead contrasting its 0.706 result only against white-bear's 0.510.
